messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Line Balancing Algorithm - Manufacturing process
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have no idea the optimisation method that has been implemented on simmer.optim module, however, you need a direct search optimisation method approach, namely, derivative free method, for identifying a local optimum at least.

On the other hand, you need to explore inside the feasible region problem, that means, if you want to identify the optimum setting of two serial queues, for example: M/M/1/n_{1} + G/M/1/n_{2}, and  n_{i} \in\{1,...,10}, for all i=1,2, and your objective function is the number of item in queue, then you optimisation problem could be:

min f(n_{1},n_{2})
subject to:
1<= n_{1} <= 10
1<= n_{2} <= 10

That is, your feasible region is a 2-dimensional box, and your optimisation method needs to explore inside the box by evaluation of the objective function and using of trial points in the feasible region.

Nowadays, I am developing an interior point direct search optimisation method for mixed integer optimisation problems, which allow me to identify a global optimum at least. This new algorithm will be applied to constrained mixer integer optimisation method problems and it will identify global optimum by trial point inside the feasible region.

For more information, please see:
Una extensión del método de Nelder Mead a problemas de optimización no lineales enteros mixtos
at https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0213131513000345

Game of Patterns: An approach for solving mixed integer nonlinear optimization problems
at http://ieomsociety.org/bogota2017/proceedings/

Game of Patterns and Genetic Algorithms Under a Comparative Study
at https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007%2F978-3-030-05983-5_7

Best regards,

Ebert

Two things:

1. With respect to "object visibility", normal attributes
(set_attribute, get_attribute) are per-arrival. On the other hand,
global attributes (set_global, get_global) are visible by all the
arrivals. Both kinds of attributes are numeric, but they can be used
to set indexes and store info in more complex global R structures when
needed.

2. What you are linking here is not the same kind of use case you
provided in your first email. "Master-slave process cooperation" has
nothing to do with any resource (the "common task" may involve some
resource, but not necessarily). This use case would be equivalent to
batch processing in simmer (see ?batch).

Iñaki
